words.gloss: to the auspicious Gaṇeśa (name of a deity)

hindi: श्री गणेश को नमस्कार।
english: Homage to the auspicious Gaṇeśa.
notes: Invocation. 'Gaṇeśa' is a divine name; nothing further is added.

hindi: धन्वन्तरि को नमस्कार।
english: Homage to Dhanvantari.
notes: Invocation; Dhanvantari kept as a name. The printed dative dhanvantaraye is a correct i-stem form.

words.gloss: putrakāmīya, relating to one who desires a son

hindi: अब इसके बाद हम पुत्रकामीय शारीर की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the putrakāmīya (relating to one who desires a son) Śārīra (relating to the body).

text_flags.why: possible: short i printed for long ī (putra-kāma + -īya)

notes: Both putrakāmīya and śārīra are accusative; the usual reading is that this is the chapter 'Putrakāmīya' of the Śārīra section, but the line does not say 'chapter'. The tokens śārīraṃvyākhyāsyāmaḥ is one printed word for śārīram vyākhyāsyāmaḥ.

hindi: ऐसा आत्रेय आदि महर्षियों ने कहा।
english: Thus, indeed, Ātreya and the other great sages said.
notes: 'ha sma' with a perfect is a past-time idiom; 'āhuḥ' is the perfect 3 pl. of √ah, 'they said'. 'Ātreya ādayaḥ' = Ātreya and others.

words.gloss: undamaged; teeth; lips; ears; nails; hair; breasts
immortals; serpents; rivers; moving things; trees; birds; stars; other; not to be looked at; frightening; names

words.gram: pres. part. f. acc. sg. an-ud-√vah

hindi: अब इक्कीस वर्ष का पुरुष ऐसी कन्या से विवाह करे जो असमान गोत्र की और असमान वंश की हो, जिसका जन्म ऐसे कुल में हुआ हो जिसमें रोग संचारी नहीं है, जो रूप, शील और लक्षणों से सम्पन्न हो, न्यून न हो, जिसके दाँत, होंठ, कान, नख, केश और स्तन नष्ट न हुए हों, जिसकी प्रकृति कोमल और रोगरहित हो, जो न कपिला हो न पिंगला, जिसके अंग न हीन हों न अधिक, जो लगभग बारह वर्ष की हो, जो देवता, सर्प, नदी, चल वस्तु, वृक्ष, पक्षी, नक्षत्र तथा अन्य न देखने योग्य और भयानक वस्तुओं के नाम धारण न करती हो, जो निर्दोष और निन्दा से रहित हो; निन्दारहित विधि से वह उसे ब्याहे।
english: Now, a man of twenty-one years should marry, by a blameless rule, a girl of unlike gotra and of unlike ancestry, born in a family in which disease is non-transmitting; endowed with beauty, conduct and marks; not deficient; whose teeth, lips, ears, nails, hair and breasts are undamaged; whose constitution (prakṛti) is gentle and free of disease; not tawny and not reddish-brown; with limbs neither deficient nor in excess; of about twelve years; not bearing names of immortals, serpents, rivers, moving things, trees, birds, stars, or of other things not to be looked at and frightening; faultless and blameless.

text_flags.why: print spacing: the final m of aniṃdyām stands at the start of the next printed token
stray m belongs to the preceding word aniṃdyām
possible: extra 'du' (or vidhinodvahet); sense 'by rule, should marry'
possible: masculine mṛdum beside feminine accusatives; ā in arogā- also doubtful

notes: Long single prose sentence; subject pumān, verb udvahet at the end. Parse points: (1) atulya = 'unlike' (the text does not say 'not of his own'); the sense is probably 'not of his own gotra and ancestry'. (2) asaṃcāri-roga-kula: literally 'disease non-transmitting, family'; the sense is probably a family without hereditary disease, not certain. (3) mṛdu-aroga-prakṛti: reading uncertain, see text_flags. (4) ahīna-adhika-aṅgī: literally 'not deficient, in excess, limbed'; the plainer sense is 'neither deficient nor excessive in limbs'. (5) deśīya = approximately. (6) the name-list: 'nakṣatrānyaprekṣyabhīṣaṇakanāmāni' could also be read nakṣatra-nāmāni, anya-aprekṣya-bhīṣaṇaka-nāmāni; the rendering 'of other things not to be looked at and frightening' is one reading. cala is rendered 'moving things'; its exact referent is not stated.

hindi: उसमें, जो सोलह वर्ष की है, पच्चीस वर्ष का पुरुष पुत्र के लिए प्रयत्न करे।
english: In her, of sixteen years, a man of twenty-five years should strive for the sake of a son.
notes: Ages are translated as printed (unit 5 says the girl is of about twelve years; this unit says sixteen). The two statements are not reconciled here. 'tasyām' refers back to the kanyā of unit 5.

hindi: क्योंकि तब वे दोनों वीर्य यानी शक्ति को प्राप्त होकर शक्ति से युक्त सन्तान को उत्पन्न करते हैं।
english: For then those two, having attained potency (vīrya), beget offspring endowed with potency.
notes: 'vīrya' is rendered 'potency' (vigor), not semen; the text does not say 'semen' here. The printed token vīryānvitamapatyaṃ is vīrya-anvitam apatyam; split into two words below.

hindi: पच्चीस वर्ष से कम आयु वाले पुरुष द्वारा सोलह वर्ष से कम आयु वाली में स्थापित गर्भ कोख में ही नाश को प्राप्त हो जाए, या अल्पायु तथा बल, आरोग्य और साधनों से हीन हो, या विकल इन्द्रियों वाला हो; और ऋतु में, पहली तीन रात्रियों में, तथा दूषित होने पर, अनुमानित पाठ पर, शुक्र और आर्तव का क्षय।
english: An embryo (garbha) placed by one of less than twenty-five years in one of less than sixteen years may reach destruction in the womb itself, or may be of short life-span, with little strength, health and means, or with defective sense organs; and in the ṛtu, in the first triad of nights, and likewise when it is vitiated, on a conjectural reading, injury of semen and menstrual blood (śukra and ārtava).

text_flags.why: possible: 'kukṣisya' is not a word; 'kukṣisthaḥ' (staying in the womb) fits sense and the following eva; th/y confusion
possible: ṃ for a; vikala-indriya 'with defective senses'
possible: final word is unclear; no sure restoration (śukra-ārtava with hati 'injury' is only a guess)

notes: Heavy sentence; the last token śukrārtavahati is unrestorable with confidence: kept unsplit and marked unclear; the translation of the end is on a conjectural reading ('injury of semen and menstrual blood'). 'ṛtau ādye ca rātritraye' is rendered literally ('in the ṛtu, and in the first triad of nights'); the intended sense (first three nights of the menstrual period) is not stated by the words. ṛtu = the woman's fertile or menstrual season (probable). The subject of 'syāt' is the embryo/child. garbha is rendered 'embryo'; 'fetus' is also possible.

hindi: वहाँ भोजन का, जो ठीक प्रकार परिणत होकर क्रम से मज्जा को प्राप्त हुआ है, सार शुक्र यानी वीर्य, पुरुष का प्रजनन द्रव, नाम पाता है।
english: There, the essence (sāra) of food that has been well transformed and has in order reached the marrow (majjan) obtains the name śukra (semen).
notes: Identification: śukra = semen (standard). majjan = marrow (probable; here the body tissue majjā, not a seed kernel). 'tatra' is taken as 'there/in that case'.

words.gloss: kalā (a membranous layer of the body; doctrinal term)
by striking together (saṃprahana; probably sexual union)
ghee; oil; honey (kṣaudra); any one of; colour

hindi: वह, दूध में घी और ईख के रस में गुड़ की तरह, शरीर में शुक्रधरा कला का आश्रय लेकर समस्त अंगों में व्याप्त होने से स्थित रहता है, और विशेषकर मज्जा, मुष्क यानी वृषण और स्तनों में; हर्ष से और संप्रहनन से प्रेरित होकर, हृदय के आवेश से, पिण्ड बनकर, अंग-अंग से निकलता है। वह सौम्य, स्निग्ध, भारी, श्वेत, मधु की गन्ध वाला, मधुर, पिच्छिल, बहुत, गाढ़ा, और घी, तेल या शहद में से किसी एक के रंग वाला शुक्र यानी वीर्य गर्भाधान के योग्य होता है।
english: That, like ghee in milk and jaggery in sugarcane juice, abides in the body, resting in the śukra-bearing kalā (a membranous layer), by pervading all the limbs, and especially in the marrow (majjā), the testicles (muṣka) and the breasts; stirred up by excitement and by saṃprahana (striking together), from the possession of the heart, having become a lump, it issues from limb to limb. That śukra (semen), gentle (saumya), unctuous, heavy, white, honey-scented, sweet, slimy, abundant, thick, and of the colour of any one of ghee, oil or honey, becomes fit for conception (garbhādhāna).

text_flags.why: possible: 'tat tu' (that, indeed) for the printed tatu
possible: 'kṣīre iva' (like in milk); ha/i confusion
possible: 'iva' printed as 'hava'; sarpiḥ + ikṣurase
possible: b for v, o for ā, ṃ lost

notes: No subject is named for the first sentence ('tat' neuter); it is read as the śukra of the next sentence. The similes 'kṣīre iva sarpiḥ, ikṣurase iva guḍaḥ' (ghee in milk, jaggery in sugarcane juice) rest on three corrections that are likely but not certain. kalā: a doctrinal term for a membranous layer or sheath; no modern equivalent forced. saṃprahana: literally a striking together; 'probably sexual union' is an interpretation, not certain. hṛdayāveśāt: 'from the possession (absorption) of the heart'; understood as emotional absorption, not certain. majjā here = marrow (body tissue). 'varṇa' is in the Sanskrit and is translated 'colour'. Identifications: śukra = semen (standard); muṣka = testicle (standard).

words.gram: pres. part. ā. n. nom. sg.

hindi: उसी प्रकार स्त्रियों का रक्त ही, हर मास गर्भकोष्ठ को प्राप्त होकर, तीन दिन बहता हुआ, आर्तव यानी रजोधर्म का रक्त कहा जाता है।
english: Likewise, the blood itself of women, month by month, having reached the garbhakoṣṭha (womb), flowing for three days, they call ārtava (menstrual blood).
notes: 'garbhakoṣṭha' = literally 'store-room (hollow) of the embryo'; modern equivalent womb/uterus (probable). 'ārtavam iti āhuḥ': they call it ārtava. 'māse māse' = every month.

words.gloss: pradara (abnormal vaginal discharge or bleeding; probable)

hindi: अतिप्रसंग से, ऋतु के अतिरिक्त समय में या ऋतु में, वही असृग्दर, प्रदर और व्यापद तथा रक्तयोनि नाम पाता है।
english: Through excessive continuation, whether out of season or in season, that very thing obtains the names asṛgdara (excessive menstrual bleeding), pradara (abnormal vaginal discharge or bleeding) and vyāpad (disorder), and the name raktayoni.

text_flags.why: possible: printed spacing shifted; the final ā is the first letter of asṛgdaram (tad eva + asṛgdaram)
initial a joins the previous printed token by sandhi (evāsṛg-)

notes: Reading: 'anṛtau ṛtau vā tad eva asṛgdaram pradaram vyāpadam ca raktayonisaṃjñām labhate'. The accusatives asṛgdaram, pradaram, vyāpadam and raktayoni-saṃjñām are taken as the names obtained; the exact relation is not certain. 'tad' refers back to ārtava of unit 11. Identification: asṛgdara, pradara = excessive menstrual or vaginal bleeding/discharge (probable; usage varies). raktayoni kept as a name (literally 'blood-womb').

hindi: उसके साधन में रक्तपित्त की चिकित्सा और गुह्य रोगों के प्रतिषेध को भी देखे।
english: In the management of that, one should look to the treatment of raktapitta (a bleeding disorder) and the remedy (pratiṣedha) for diseases of the private parts (guhya-roga).
notes: raktapitta kept in Sanskrit; modern equivalent a bleeding disorder (probable, not a single modern disease). guhya = private (genital) parts. 'īkṣeta' = should look to / consult.

words.gram: pres. part. ā. n. nom. sg.
pres. part. ā. n. nom. sg.
pres. part. ā. f. gen. sg.
pres. part. caus. √dṛś, n. nom. sg.

hindi: जिनके मार्ग वात और कफ से ढके हों उनका, न बहता हुआ, पित्त बढ़ाने वाले उपचारों से वह बहता हुआ, शुक्र के साथ या शुक्र के बिना, जीवरहित, वात बढ़ाने वाले का सेवन करती हुई स्त्री का, गर्भ के लक्षण दिखाता हुआ, गुल्म वाला हो जाता है; वहाँ गुल्म की चिकित्सा को देखे।
english: Of those whose passages are covered by Vāta and Kapha, not flowing; when that flows through Pitta-increasing measures, with semen or without semen, devoid of life, of a woman who resorts to Vāta-increasing (ones), showing the signs of pregnancy, it becomes one with gulma (an abdominal lump); in that case one should look to the treatment of gulma.

text_flags.why: possible: 'aśukam' is not a word; opposite of saṃśukram 'with śukra' is aśukram 'without śukra'

notes: The sentence is loose and its syntax is not certain. The words are translated in the printed order. It appears that the blood (ārtava) of unit 11 is the unstated subject, retained and later flowing, and that what results shows signs of pregnancy and is lifeless (jīva-rahita); the reading 'gulmī bhavati' = 'becomes gulmin' (a person or thing with gulma) is not decided. gulma kept in Sanskrit; commonly an abdominal lump or mass (standard rendering).

words.gloss: Vāta; belly (vātodara: Vāta-belly, abdominal swelling from Vāta; probable)

hindi: कभी गर्भवती स्त्री में भी वातोदर यानी वात से पेट का फूलना हो जाता है; वह वात को शान्त करने वालों से शान्त हो जाता है।
english: Or sometimes, in a pregnant (woman) indeed, vātodara (Vāta-belly: abdominal swelling from Vāta) occurs; that subsides with Vāta-pacifying (ones).
notes: 'garbhaiva' is ambiguous: garbhā eva ('a pregnant woman indeed'; taken here) or garbha eva ('the embryo itself'); garbha iva would give garbheva, so 'as if pregnant' is not read. vātodara: Vāta-belly, a swelling of the belly attributed to Vāta; modern equivalent probably abdominal distension (probable). 'vāta-aupaśamana' = Vāta-pacifying; the noun they qualify is not stated.

hindi: वही आर्तव कभी सौम्य, बृंहण स्वभाव वाले आहार और विहारों से रुका हुआ, उपद्रवरहित ही उदर को, मानो गर्भ से अधिष्ठित हो, बढ़ा देता है।
english: That very ārtava (menstrual blood), sometimes held back by gentle diets and regimens of a bulk-promoting (bṛṃhaṇa) nature, increases the belly (udara), free of complications, as if occupied by an embryo.

text_flags.why: dv for dh: OCR/print confusion; vardhayati 'makes grow'

notes: Subject is ārtava; stambhita is taken with ārtava, anupadrava with udara (belly); the grouping of these adjectives is not certain. bṛṃhaṇa = bulk-promoting, nourishing (doctrinal term). 'udara' is rendered 'belly'.

hindi: जिससे मूढ़ लोग उस अगर्भिणी को गर्भिणी कहते हैं।
english: Because of which the deluded call her, who is not pregnant, pregnant.

text_flags.why: possible: the final -m and -ṇī- seem lost; agarbhīm would also scan

notes: 'yena' is taken as 'by which / because of which' (the appearance described in 16).

hindi: तब विपरीतों से या संयोग से रक्त के बहने पर गर्भ का शरीर न देखते हुए अज्ञ लोग कहते हैं कि भूतों द्वारा हर लिया गया।
english: Then, when the blood flows through contrary (ones) or by chance, not seeing the body of the embryo, the ignorant say: 'carried off by beings (bhūta)'.
notes: 'viparītaiḥ' (contrary) has no stated noun; it probably refers to the opposite measures to those in unit 16 (not certain). 'bhūta' = being, spirit; kept literal.

hindi: क्योंकि राक्षसों द्वारा ओज का अपहरण सम्भव है, परन्तु शरीर का नहीं, अनिष्ट होने से या असमर्थता से।
english: Since the taking away of ojas (vital essence) by rakṣas (demons) occurs, but not of the body, from undesirability or from incapacity.

text_flags.why: possible: initial a of aśakteḥ lost in the printed ād-ś

notes: Elliptical: 'apaharaṇam' (taking away) is carried over to 'of the body'. Whose undesirability or incapacity is meant is not stated.

hindi: क्योंकि इच्छा और शक्ति के प्रवृत्त होने पर उपलब्धि नहीं होती, और किसी के देह का मनुष्यों द्वारा अपहरण नहीं देखा जाता।
english: For when desire and power are engaged, there is no perception, and the removal of anyone's body by humans is not seen.

text_flags.why: possible: initial r looks extra; upalabdhi 'perception' fits the sense; rūpa-labdhi is not clear

notes: The grammar of 'icchāśaktayor hi pravṛtte' is uncertain (locative dual absolute). The reading is not firm.

hindi: और यदि कुछ अत्यधिक शक्ति से युक्त लोग देखे हुए को भी लाँघकर गर्भ के शरीर के उत्क्षेप में प्रवृत्त होते हैं, तब कैसे भला अनुमानित पाठ पर उसकी माताओं की उपेक्षा करेंगे।
english: And if some, endowed with excessive power, passing beyond even what is seen, proceed to cast off the body of the embryo, then how indeed would the prāptaviśarāḥ (unclear, on a conjectural reading) neglect its mothers?

text_flags.why: possible: visarga lost before garbhasya
the word prāptaviśarāḥ is unclear; no sure restoration; the rest tad-jananīḥ upekṣeran is clear

notes: Damaged or unclear word 'prāptaviśarāḥ' kept unsplit; it is probably an adjective or subject of 'upekṣeran' (the beings said to take the embryo?), but this is a conjecture and the translation of that part is on a conjectural reading. 'ākṣepa' = casting off or removal. 'dṛṣṭam api samullaṅghya' = literally 'even having transgressed what is seen'. The doubled tt in 'pravarttante' is normalised.

words.gram: pres. part. pass. vi-√rañj, n. acc. sg.

hindi: आर्तव को फिर, जो खरगोश के रक्त और लाख के रस के समान हो और धोने पर रंग छोड़ता जाए, शुद्ध कहते हैं।
english: Ārtava (menstrual blood), moreover, which resembles hare's blood and lac-juice and, when washed, loses its colour, they call pure.
notes: lākṣā = lac, the resin dye of the lac insect (standard). 'śaśarudhira-lākṣārasa' is read as a dvandva (hare's blood and lac-juice), not decided. 'virajyamāna' = losing colour (becoming decoloured).
